properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

Anthony's distillation (2026-07-28) is that the roadmap is a SATISFACTION SCHEDULE — requirements mapped to the epoch or increment where they are satisfied — and his own verbs carry three modalities: requirements "ARE satisfied" in epoch 1, "are EXPECTED to be satisfied" in increment 3, KPP 1 "is REQUIRED to be satisfied" by epoch 27.

THE OBSERVATION THAT MATTERS MOST: the three do not want the same treatment, and one of them must not be stored at all.

ARE SATISFIED — must be COMPUTED, never recorded. `req:completion-computed` is accepted and says whether intent has been delivered is computed from the golden thread and never asserted. A stored "requirement A was satisfied at epoch 1" would be exactly the assertion that requirement forbids, and it would rot the moment the thread moved. The backward direction already works; it needs a way to ask "as of epoch N", not a place to write the answer.

EXPECTED TO BE SATISFIED — the vocabulary already exists. `ANTICIPATES` is declared from `*` to `*` with a `confidence` float 0.0–1.0 and the hint "Source plans for or foreshadows a future target need." `req:plans-move-honestly` already named it as the hook. So `req:X --ANTICIPATES(confidence)--> epoch:3` may be the whole mechanism, with confidence decaying by horizon per the Black-Scholes framing.

REQUIRED TO BE SATISFIED BY — different in kind, not degree. Missing an EXPECTED date is a surprise to record; missing a REQUIRED date is a VIOLATION to compute. This is the scheduling face of a KPP: `req:inviolable-intent` already computes content violations, and this would give it a deadline dimension. Open whether that is a distinct edge type, or `ANTICIPATES` with a binding flag — and the honest test is the one this project keeps applying: which one lets a computation read it without inventing a value nobody set.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING, having looked: less than the requirement's ambition suggests. The capability view's forward half is expressible today (`Release.status: planned`). The schedule edge exists (`ANTICIPATES` with confidence). What does not exist is (1) a `DesignEpoch.epoch_type` value meaning "has not happened yet", (2) any reader of `ANTICIPATES` — it is declared and nothing computes over it, which is `req:defaults-do-not-assert`'s sibling defect of declared-but-unread vocabulary, and (3) an ARRIVAL operation: someone must be able to say an epoch arrived, at which point the planned-versus-delivered delta is computed and the pin recorded.

Arrival is where the three requirements meet: it is when a planned epoch stops being a claim (`req:epochs-can-be-planned`), acquires a git pin (`req:graph-indexes-snapshots`), and produces the delta between what was planned and what landed (`req:plans-move-honestly`). It is also the natural moment for `cap:changelog-view` to render, since the changelog between two arrivals is the same delta in prose.
properties.name: OPEN — how the satisfaction schedule records ARE / EXPECTED / REQUIRED-BY
properties.rationale:
Anthony's atom, recorded in his own verbs because the three modalities are carried by the verbs and would be lost in a paraphrase.

The "ARE satisfied must not be stored" point is the one worth not losing: it is the difference between a roadmap that reports and a roadmap that claims, and this design already has an accepted requirement forbidding the second. Everything else here is options; that one is a constraint the existing design imposes on any shape chosen.
